questions.text: What do Christians call the belief that God is one God in three persons?

feedback: The Incarnation is the belief that God became human in Jesus
The Resurrection is the belief that Jesus rose from the dead
The Atonement is the belief that Jesus' death restored the relationship between God and humanity

questions.solution: Christians believe in the Trinity: one God who is Father, Son and Holy Spirit
questions.hint: Think of a word linked to the number three

questions.text: Christians believe God is three persons: the Father, the Son and one more. Name the third person of the Trinity.
questions.solution: The third person of the Trinity is the Holy Spirit
questions.hint: Christians believe this person came to the apostles at Pentecost

questions.text: Which Christian festival celebrates the belief that Jesus rose from the dead?

feedback: Christmas celebrates the birth of Jesus
Pentecost remembers the Holy Spirit coming to the apostles
Advent is the time of preparation before Christmas

questions.solution: At Easter Christians celebrate their belief in the resurrection of Jesus
questions.hint: It comes at the end of Holy Week

questions.text: Many Christians share bread and wine to remember Jesus' Last Supper. Give one name for this service.
questions.solution: This service is called the Eucharist, Holy Communion, Mass, the Lord's Supper or the Divine Liturgy, depending on the church
questions.hint: Different churches use different names; one comes from the Greek word for thanksgiving

questions.text: In Christian belief, what is the Incarnation?

options: The Holy Spirit coming to the apostles
feedback: That is the Resurrection
That is the Ascension
That is Pentecost

questions.solution: Christians believe that in the Incarnation God became human as Jesus, fully God and fully human
questions.hint: Christians celebrate this at Christmas

questions.text: What is the Christian ceremony in which a person is welcomed into the Church using water? Give the term.

feedback.baptist: Baptists are a Christian denomination — give the name of the ceremony

questions.solution: Baptism uses water as a sign of being cleansed from sin and welcomed into the Church
questions.hint: Jesus received this from John in the River Jordan

questions.text: How many sacraments does the Catholic Church recognise?

feedback: Most Protestant churches recognise two sacraments: baptism and the Eucharist

questions.solution: The Catholic and Orthodox Churches recognise seven sacraments, including baptism, the Eucharist and marriage
questions.hint: Most Protestant churches recognise fewer than the Catholic Church does

questions.text: Which statement describes believers' baptism, as practised in Baptist churches?

options: People old enough to choose faith for themselves are baptised, often by full immersion
Babies are baptised using water from a font
feedback: That describes infant baptism

questions.solution: Believers' baptism is for people who can make their own commitment, usually by full immersion in a pool
questions.hint: Think about who makes the promises in believers' baptism

questions.text: What do Catholics call the belief that the bread and wine become the body and blood of Christ during Mass?

feedback: The Incarnation is God becoming human in Jesus
Atonement is the restored relationship between God and humanity through Jesus' death
The Ascension is Jesus returning to heaven

questions.solution: Catholics believe in transubstantiation: the bread and wine truly become the body and blood of Christ
questions.hint: The word contains 'substance', meaning what something really is

questions.text: What is the period of 40 days before Easter called, when many Christians fast or give something up? Give the term.

feedback.Advent: Advent is the time of preparation before Christmas

questions.solution: Lent lasts 40 days and remembers Jesus' time fasting in the wilderness
questions.hint: It begins on Ash Wednesday

questions.text: Which French town do many Catholics visit on pilgrimage because Bernadette said she saw visions of Mary there in 1858? Give the name.
questions.solution: Many Catholics visit Lourdes, and some sick pilgrims bathe in its waters hoping for healing
questions.hint: It is in the foothills of the Pyrenees mountains

questions.text: Which Greek word do Christians use for selfless, unconditional love?

feedback: Koinonia means fellowship or community
Ecumenism means different Christian churches working together
Evangelism means spreading the Christian faith

questions.solution: Agape is the selfless love Christians believe God shows and which they try to show others
questions.hint: It is the kind of love Jesus taught in the parable of the Good Samaritan

questions.text: A Christian family has their baby baptised at a font in an Anglican church. Which type of baptism is this?

feedback: Believers' baptism is for people old enough to choose for themselves
Confirmation is when a person confirms the promises made at their baptism
Ordination is when someone becomes a priest or minister

questions.solution: Infant baptism welcomes a baby into the Church; parents and godparents make promises for the child
questions.hint: Think about who makes the promises when a baby is baptised

questions.text: A church runs a food bank and visits lonely elderly people in its area. What does this show about the Church's role?
questions.solution: Many churches serve their local community, following Jesus' teaching to love your neighbour
questions.hint: Think about who benefits and where they live

questions.text: Which of these Christian organisations works mainly to reduce poverty in developing countries?

feedback: Street Pastors work on the streets of UK towns at night
The Trussell Trust runs food banks in the UK
Alpha is a course introducing people to the Christian faith

questions.solution: Christian Aid works in developing countries on poverty, emergencies and fair trade
questions.hint: Its name contains a word meaning help given to people in need

questions.text: A Christian says: 'Jesus' death mended the relationship between God and humanity.' Which belief is this?
questions.solution: Atonement is the belief that Jesus' death and resurrection restored the relationship between God and people
questions.hint: The word can be split into at-one-ment

questions.text: Which Christian festival, seven weeks after Easter Sunday, remembers the Holy Spirit coming to the apostles? Give the name.
questions.solution: At Pentecost Christians remember the Holy Spirit coming to the apostles, often called the birthday of the Church
questions.hint: Its name comes from the Greek word for 'fiftieth', as it is the 50th day of the Easter season

questions.text: Christians believe Jesus was taken up into heaven 40 days after the resurrection. What is this event called? Give the term.

feedback.Assumption: The Assumption is the Catholic belief about Mary being taken into heaven

questions.solution: The Ascension is Jesus returning to heaven 40 days after the resurrection
questions.hint: The word means going up

questions.text: John's Gospel says that 'the Word was made flesh' and lived among people. Which Christian belief does this support?

feedback: Transubstantiation is about the bread and wine at Mass
Purgatory is a Catholic belief about life after death
Pentecost is about the Holy Spirit coming to the apostles

questions.solution: Christians read 'the Word' as Jesus, so this verse supports the belief that God became human
questions.hint: Flesh means a human body

questions.text: In a survey of one church, 60% of members go to a service that follows set prayers from a book, and 40% go to informal worship with spontaneous prayer. What type of worship do the 60% attend?

feedback: Non-liturgical worship is less formal, with no fixed order
Charismatic worship is lively and spontaneous, led by the Spirit

questions.solution: Liturgical worship follows a set pattern of prayers and readings, often from a service book
questions.hint: Think about which type of worship uses a set order

questions.text: Which pair of sacraments do most Protestant churches recognise?

options: Confirmation and anointing of the sick

questions.solution: Most Protestants recognise only baptism and the Eucharist, because Jesus commanded both in the Gospels
questions.hint: Think about the two sacraments Jesus took part in or commanded in the Gospels

questions.text: Catholics believe some people who die in God's friendship are purified before entering heaven. What is this state called?
questions.solution: Catholics believe purgatory is a state of cleansing before entering heaven
questions.hint: The word is related to 'purge', meaning to cleanse

questions.text: In Matthew's Gospel, Jesus says those who fed the hungry, gave water to the thirsty and welcomed strangers did it for him. Which parable is this? Give its name.

accept: Parable of the Sheep and the Goats
Parable of the Sheep and Goats

questions.solution: In the Parable of the Sheep and the Goats, Jesus teaches that caring for people in need is caring for him
questions.hint: The people are divided like a shepherd separating two kinds of animals

questions.text: Describe two ways Christians celebrate Easter.

rubric.model_answer: Many Christians attend church on Easter Sunday to celebrate their belief that Jesus rose from the dead. Some churches hold a vigil on Saturday night, where a Paschal candle is lit to symbolise Jesus as the light of the world. Before Easter, many Christians remember Holy Week, for example with Good Friday services about the crucifixion. Many also give Easter eggs as a symbol of new life.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one practice (e.g. Easter Sunday service)
1 mark: explains its meaning or detail
1 mark: identifies a second practice (e.g. vigil, Paschal candle, Easter eggs)
1 mark: explains its meaning or detail

questions.solution: Church services, the Easter vigil and symbols of new life are all part of Easter
questions.hint: Think about Easter Sunday services and the symbols used

questions.text: Which statement about why the resurrection is important to Christians is accurate?

options: All Christians believe Jesus never died
Christians believe the resurrection happened at Pentecost
Christians believe it shows Jesus was only a prophet
Many Christians believe it shows Jesus defeated death and offers eternal life

questions.solution: Many Christians believe the resurrection shows Jesus was the Son of God and that death is not the end
questions.hint: Think about what Christians believe the resurrection means for life after death

questions.text: Why do some Christians, such as Quakers, not celebrate sacraments?

options: They believe God's grace can be experienced directly, without outward rituals
They believe sacraments are only for priests
They believe the Bible forbids the use of water
They only worship on Christmas Day

questions.solution: Quakers believe all of life can be sacred and that God can be met directly in silent worship
questions.hint: Think about the Quaker style of silent worship

questions.text: Which statement about Christian views on the Eucharist is accurate?

options: All Christians believe the bread and wine are only symbols
Catholics believe in transubstantiation, while many Protestants see the bread and wine as symbols
Every church celebrates the Eucharist only once a year

questions.solution: Christians disagree about the Eucharist: Catholics believe Christ is truly present, while many Protestants see it as a memorial
questions.hint: Compare Catholic and Protestant beliefs about the bread and wine

questions.text: Why is pilgrimage important to many Christians?

options: The Bible requires every Christian to visit Rome
Pilgrimage is one of the Five Pillars of Christianity
It can strengthen their faith and bring them closer to God
feedback: The Five Pillars are duties in Islam; Hajj is the Muslim pilgrimage

questions.solution: Many Christians see pilgrimage as a spiritual journey to grow closer to God, pray and reflect
questions.hint: Think about why a believer might travel to a holy place

questions.text: Which statement about the Christian belief in salvation is accurate?

options: Christians believe salvation is earned only by going on pilgrimage
Christians believe salvation is impossible for anyone
Christians believe salvation comes from the Five Pillars
Many Christians believe salvation comes through God's grace and faith in Jesus

questions.solution: Many Christians believe people are saved from sin by God's grace through faith in Jesus
questions.hint: Think about the role of grace, a gift from God that is not earned

questions.text: Explain two Christian teachings that encourage Christians to support people living in poverty.

rubric.model_answer: In the Parable of the Sheep and the Goats, Jesus teaches that whoever feeds the hungry or welcomes strangers does it for him, so many Christians believe caring for the poor is serving Jesus. In the Parable of the Good Samaritan, a Samaritan cares for an injured stranger, which teaches Christians to love their neighbour, whoever they are. Many Christians therefore give to charities such as Christian Aid.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies a relevant teaching (e.g. Sheep and the Goats)
1 mark: explains how it applies to poverty
1 mark: identifies a second teaching (e.g. Good Samaritan, love your neighbour)
1 mark: explains how it applies to poverty

questions.solution: Jesus' parables teach Christians to care for those in need as if caring for him
questions.hint: Think of two parables about caring for people in need

questions.text: Which Arabic word do Muslims use for the belief in the oneness of God? Give the term.
questions.solution: Tawhid is the Muslim belief that Allah is one and unique
questions.hint: It is the most important belief in Islam and begins with the letter T

questions.text: How many daily prayers make up salah for Muslims?
questions.solution: Muslims perform five daily prayers; many Shi'a Muslims combine them into three sessions
questions.hint: Think about the prayer times from dawn until night

questions.text: Which city do Muslims face when they pray?

feedback: Madinah is the city the Prophet moved to in 622 CE
The first Muslims faced Jerusalem before the direction was changed
Karbala is important to Shi'a Muslims as the place where Husayn died

questions.solution: Muslims face the Ka'bah in Makkah; this direction is called the qiblah
questions.hint: It is the city where the Ka'bah stands

questions.text: What is the name of the Muslim holy book? Give the name.
questions.solution: Muslims believe the Qur'an is the word of Allah, revealed to the Prophet Muhammad
questions.hint: Muslims believe it was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad by the angel Jibril

questions.text: Which pillar of Islam involves giving 2.5% of savings to people in need?

feedback: Sawm is fasting during Ramadan
Salah is prayer
Hajj is the pilgrimage to Makkah

questions.solution: Zakah is giving 2.5% of savings above a set amount (nisab) each year to people in need
questions.hint: It purifies wealth by sharing it

questions.text: What is the Muslim month of fasting called? Give the name.
questions.solution: Muslims fast from dawn to sunset during Ramadan
questions.hint: It is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar

questions.text: Which statement about the division between Sunni and Shi'a Muslims is accurate?

options: Sunni Muslims believe Ali was the first caliph
Shi'a Muslims do not use the Qur'an
Sunni Muslims do not perform salah
Shi'a Muslims believe Ali should have succeeded the Prophet Muhammad
feedback: Sunni Muslims accept Abu Bakr as the first caliph; Ali was the fourth

questions.solution: After the Prophet's death in 632 CE, Sunni Muslims accepted Abu Bakr as leader, while Shi'a Muslims believe Ali should have led
questions.hint: The split was about who should lead after the Prophet's death

questions.text: What is wudu?

feedback: The call to prayer is the adhan
The direction of prayer is the qiblah
That is zakah or sadaqah

questions.solution: Wudu is the ritual washing of the hands, mouth, face, arms, head and feet before salah
questions.hint: It prepares a Muslim to stand before Allah in prayer

questions.text: Which Muslim festival marks the end of Ramadan?

feedback: Eid ul-Adha takes place during Hajj and remembers Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son
Ashura is on the 10th of Muharram
Laylat al-Qadr remembers the first revelation of the Qur'an

questions.solution: Eid ul-Fitr celebrates the end of the month of fasting
questions.hint: Its name includes a word linked to breaking the fast

questions.text: Which angel do Muslims believe revealed the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad? Give the name.
questions.solution: Muslims believe the angel Jibril revealed the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad over about 23 years
questions.hint: This angel also appears in the Jewish and Christian scriptures

questions.text: What is the name of the pilgrimage to Makkah that every Muslim who is able should make at least once? Give the name.

feedback.Umrah: Umrah is a shorter pilgrimage that can be made at any time of year

questions.solution: Hajj is the fifth pillar of Islam, made in the month of Dhul Hijjah
questions.hint: It takes place in the last month of the Islamic year

questions.text: What is the Shahadah?

options: The festival at the end of Hajj
The Muslim name for the Gospel
The niche in a mosque wall
feedback: The Gospel is called the Injil
The niche showing the direction of Makkah is the mihrab

questions.solution: The Shahadah declares that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is the messenger of Allah
questions.hint: It is the first pillar of Islam

questions.text: A Shi'a Muslim gives one-fifth (20%) of their surplus income each year as a religious duty. What is this called?

feedback: Zakah is 2.5% of savings
Sadaqah is voluntary charity with no fixed amount
Sawm is fasting

questions.solution: Khums is one of the Ten Obligatory Acts of Shi'a Islam: one-fifth of surplus income
questions.hint: The word comes from the Arabic for one-fifth

questions.text: During Hajj, pilgrims walk seven times around a cube-shaped building. What is this building called?

feedback: The Dome of the Rock is in Jerusalem
The mihrab is a niche in a mosque wall
Mount Arafat is a hill where pilgrims stand and pray

questions.solution: Pilgrims perform tawaf, circling the Ka'bah in Makkah seven times anticlockwise
questions.hint: Muslims all over the world face this building when they pray

questions.text: A Muslim student tries hard every day to resist temptation and live as they believe Allah wants. Which idea is this an example of?

feedback: Lesser jihad is the struggle to defend Islam, with strict conditions
The Hijrah was the Prophet's journey from Makkah to Madinah in 622 CE
Akhirah means life after death

questions.solution: Greater jihad is the personal struggle to live as a good Muslim
questions.hint: Jihad means struggle; think about which kind is personal

questions.text: During Hajj, pilgrims walk between two hills, Safa and Marwah. Which story are they remembering?

options: The first revelation of the Qur'an
Hajar's search for water for her son Isma'il
The death of Husayn at Karbala

questions.solution: Pilgrims remember Hajar running between the hills looking for water, before the Zamzam spring appeared
questions.hint: The story is about a mother and a baby in the desert

questions.text: What is the name of the night on which Muslims believe the Qur'an was first revealed to the Prophet Muhammad? Give the name.
questions.solution: Muslims believe the first revelation came on Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Power, in 610 CE
questions.hint: It falls during the last ten nights of Ramadan

questions.text: What is the call to prayer made from a mosque called? Give the term.
questions.solution: The adhan is called by the muezzin (mu'adhin) five times a day to call Muslims to prayer
questions.hint: It is called out five times a day, often from a minaret

questions.text: The Shahadah says: 'There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the messenger of Allah.' Many Shi'a Muslims add a phrase about which person?
questions.solution: Many Shi'a Muslims add that Ali is the friend (wali) of Allah
questions.hint: Think about who Shi'a Muslims believe should have led after the Prophet

questions.text: Sunni Muslims have Six Articles of Faith; Shi'a Muslims have the Five Roots of Usul ad-Din. Which belief is one of the Five Roots but NOT one of the Six Articles?
questions.solution: Imamah, the belief in the Imams as leaders after the Prophet, is a Shi'a root; the other three are among the Six Articles
questions.hint: Look for the belief that is special to Shi'a Islam

questions.text: A Muslim gives money to a stranger in need, without being asked, as well as paying zakah. What is this voluntary charity called?

feedback: Khums is a Shi'a duty of one-fifth of surplus income
The question says this is as well as zakah

questions.solution: Sadaqah is voluntary charity, given at any time and in any amount
questions.hint: This charity has no fixed amount

questions.text: A Muslim has £10,000 of savings above the nisab, held for a year. How much zakah should they pay at 2.5%?

feedback: That is 0.25% — check the decimal point
That is 25% — check the decimal point
That is 10%

questions.hint: Find 1% first, then multiply by 2.5

questions.text: What is the event in 622 CE called, when the Prophet Muhammad moved from Makkah to Madinah? Give the term.

feedback.hijjah: Dhu al-Hijjah is the month of the Hajj pilgrimage — the migration in 622 CE has a different name

questions.solution: The Hijrah (migration) to Madinah in 622 CE marks the start of the Islamic calendar
questions.hint: The Islamic calendar counts its years from this event

questions.text: Describe two things Muslims do during Hajj.

rubric.model_answer: Pilgrims enter ihram, a state of purity: men wear two simple white cloths and women wear plain, modest clothes, which many Muslims see as showing that everyone is equal before Allah. They perform tawaf, walking seven times anticlockwise around the Ka'bah in Makkah. They also stand on the plain of Arafat praying for forgiveness, collect pebbles at Muzdalifah and throw them at pillars in Mina to reject the devil.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one practice (e.g. tawaf)
1 mark: detail or meaning
1 mark: identifies a second practice (e.g. ihram, Arafat, stoning the pillars)
1 mark: detail or meaning

questions.solution: Ihram, tawaf, standing at Arafat and stoning the pillars are all parts of Hajj
questions.hint: Think about what pilgrims wear and what they do at the Ka'bah

questions.text: Which statement about how Sunni and Shi'a Muslims pray salah is accurate?

options: Shi'a Muslims pray only once a day
Sunni Muslims do not pray on Fridays
Many Shi'a Muslims combine the five daily prayers into three sessions

questions.solution: Both pray five daily prayers, but many Shi'a Muslims combine them into three sessions
questions.hint: Both groups pray the same number of prayers

questions.text: Why do many Muslims believe fasting during Ramadan is important?

options: It builds self-discipline and helps them remember people in poverty
Only children are required to fast
Fasting replaces the need for prayer
feedback: Children, the ill, pregnant women and travellers do not have to fast

questions.solution: Many Muslims believe sawm brings them closer to Allah, builds self-control and creates sympathy for the hungry
questions.hint: Think about how going without food might change the way a person thinks

questions.text: Which statement about the Muslim belief in akhirah is accurate?

options: Muslims believe there is no life after death
Muslims believe people will be judged by Allah and rewarded in Jannah or punished in Jahannam
Muslims believe everyone is reborn as an animal
Muslims believe only prophets will be judged

questions.solution: Muslims believe that on the Day of Judgement everyone will be judged and sent to paradise (Jannah) or hell (Jahannam)
questions.hint: Akhirah means life after death

questions.text: Which statement about lesser jihad is accurate, according to Muslim teaching?

options: Anyone can declare lesser jihad at any time
Lesser jihad is another name for the Hajj
Lesser jihad needs a just cause and a proper authority, and must not harm civilians
Lesser jihad means the personal struggle to resist temptation
feedback: That describes greater jihad

questions.solution: Muslim teaching sets strict conditions for lesser jihad: a just cause, proper authority and protection of civilians
questions.hint: Think about the rules for when fighting is allowed

questions.text: Which statement about the Qur'an is accurate, according to Muslim belief?

options: The Qur'an contains the Prophet Muhammad's own ideas
The Qur'an replaced the need for salah
The Qur'an was first written in Greek
The Qur'an is the final revelation from Allah, revealed in Arabic

questions.solution: Muslims believe the Qur'an is Allah's final revelation, given in Arabic to the Prophet Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets
questions.hint: Muslims believe it came from Allah through the angel Jibril

questions.text: Explain two reasons why the Five Pillars are important to Sunni Muslims.

rubric.model_answer: First, many Muslims believe Allah has commanded the Five Pillars, so performing them shows submission to Allah; for example, salah five times a day keeps Allah at the centre of daily life. Second, they unite the ummah, the worldwide Muslim community: all Muslims face Makkah to pray, fast together in Ramadan and meet as equals on Hajj. Zakah also supports people in poverty and purifies wealth.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies a reason (e.g. obeying Allah)
1 mark: explains it with an example
1 mark: identifies a second reason (e.g. uniting the ummah)
1 mark: explains it with an example

questions.solution: The pillars show obedience to Allah and unite Muslims worldwide
questions.hint: Think about the link between the pillars and Allah, and between the pillars and other Muslims

questions.text: Which scientist proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection in 1859? Give the surname.
questions.solution: Charles Darwin set out evolution by natural selection in On the Origin of Species (1859)
questions.hint: He wrote On the Origin of Species after a voyage on HMS Beagle

questions.text: Which scientific theory says the universe began from a single point that expanded about 13.8 billion years ago?

feedback: Evolution explains how life developed, not how the universe began
Creationism is the belief that God created the world as Genesis describes
Steady State theory said the universe had no beginning

questions.solution: The Big Bang theory says the universe expanded from a tiny, very hot, dense point
questions.hint: Its name describes a sudden beginning

questions.text: What does 'sanctity of life' mean?

options: The belief that life is only valuable if it is enjoyable
The belief that life is sacred or holy, often as a gift from God
The belief that animals have no value
The belief that people should choose when to die
feedback: That is closer to the idea of quality of life

questions.solution: Sanctity of life is the belief that all human life is sacred and precious
questions.hint: Sanctity comes from a Latin word meaning holy

questions.text: What term describes the idea that humans have a duty to look after the world for God? Give the term.

feedback.dominion: Dominion means having authority over the Earth; the duty to care for it is a different idea

questions.solution: Stewardship is the duty to care for the world on God's behalf
questions.hint: A person with this role looks after something for its owner

questions.text: What is the term for ending a person's life painlessly to relieve suffering from an incurable illness?
questions.solution: Euthanasia means a gentle or easy death, and religious believers disagree about it
questions.hint: The word comes from Greek words meaning good death

questions.text: What is the term for the belief that after death the soul is reborn in a new body? Give the term.
questions.solution: Hindus and Sikhs believe in reincarnation; Buddhists speak of rebirth
questions.hint: Hindus believe this happens to the atman until it reaches moksha

questions.text: Which statement correctly describes 'dominion' and 'stewardship'?

options: Dominion means caring for nature; stewardship means owning it
Stewardship is a Hindu belief about rebirth
Dominion means having authority over nature; stewardship means caring for it

questions.solution: Genesis gives humans dominion (rule) over nature and also the role of stewards who care for it
questions.hint: Think about a ruler and a caretaker

questions.text: When does voluntary euthanasia take place?

options: When the person who is ill asks for their life to be ended
When doctors decide for a person who cannot communicate
When treatment is stopped without anyone being asked
feedback: That describes non-voluntary euthanasia

questions.solution: Voluntary euthanasia is at the request of the person who is ill
questions.hint: Voluntary means by choice

questions.text: Who first proposed the idea that became the Big Bang theory, and was also a Catholic priest?

feedback: Darwin's theory was evolution
Richard Dawkins is a biologist known for his atheist views

questions.solution: Georges Lemaître, a Belgian priest and scientist, proposed the expanding universe in the 1920s
questions.hint: He was a Belgian scientist

questions.text: What is the name for a place that cares for people who are dying, aiming to make their last days comfortable? Give the term.
questions.solution: Hospices give care and pain relief to people who are terminally ill and support their families
questions.hint: Cicely Saunders opened the first modern one in London in 1967

questions.text: Which word is used for the idea that living things have developed gradually over millions of years from simpler forms? Give the term.
questions.solution: Evolution is the scientific theory that species change gradually over time
questions.hint: It works through natural selection

questions.text: What is the 'quality of life' argument?

options: The idea that life is sacred as a gift from God
The belief in life after death
The idea that how good or bearable a life is matters when making decisions about it
The idea that animals have souls
feedback: That is the sanctity of life argument

questions.solution: The quality of life argument looks at how much pain, happiness and independence a person has
questions.hint: Think about the word quality

questions.text: A Christian recycles, saves energy and campaigns against pollution because she believes the world belongs to God. Which belief is she acting on?
questions.solution: She is acting as a steward, caring for God's creation
questions.hint: Think about who she believes the world belongs to

questions.text: A Hindu does not eat meat because they believe in not harming living beings. What is this principle called?

feedback: Karma is the belief that actions have consequences
Moksha is release from the cycle of rebirth
Samsara is the cycle of birth, death and rebirth

questions.solution: Ahimsa is the principle of non-violence towards all living beings
questions.hint: The word means non-violence

questions.text: At a patient's request, a doctor stops a treatment that is keeping them alive and lets them die naturally. Which term is sometimes used for this?

feedback: Active euthanasia means deliberately doing something to end a life
Non-voluntary means the person could not ask; here the patient asked

questions.solution: Withdrawing treatment so a patient dies naturally is called passive euthanasia
questions.hint: Is the doctor doing something to end life, or stopping treatment?

questions.text: A Christian argues that God created the world in six days exactly as Genesis says. Which view of the Bible is this?
questions.solution: Reading Genesis as exactly true word for word is a literal interpretation
questions.hint: Think about reading the words exactly as they are written

questions.text: Genesis 1:28 says humans should rule over the fish, the birds and every living creature. What is this authority called? Give the term.

feedback.stewardship: Stewardship is the duty to care for the world; ruling over it is a different word

questions.solution: Dominion is the authority over nature that many Christians believe God gave humans
questions.hint: It comes from the Latin word dominus, meaning lord or master

questions.text: A Buddhist believes that a person's actions affect what happens to them in this life and the next. What is this law of cause and effect called? Give the term.
questions.solution: Karma (kamma) is the law that intentional actions have consequences
questions.hint: It is a Sanskrit word also used by Hindus and Sikhs

questions.text: Psalm 24 says: 'The earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof.' Which belief does this verse support?

options: Humans own the Earth and can do what they like
The universe began with the Big Bang
Humans should care for the Earth, as it belongs to God

questions.solution: If the Earth belongs to God, humans are stewards who must look after it
questions.hint: Think about who the verse says owns the earth

questions.text: A survey asked 200 people if they believe in life after death: 110 said yes, 60 said no and 30 were unsure. What percentage said yes?

feedback: 45% is the percentage who did not say yes

questions.hint: Divide the number who said yes by the total number asked

questions.text: Many Christians see no conflict between science and religion. Which statement describes their view?

options: The universe is 6,000 years old and evolution is false
God caused the Big Bang, and evolution is how God created life
There is no God, and the Big Bang happened by chance

questions.solution: Many Christians accept the Big Bang and evolution as the way God created the universe and life
questions.hint: Think about how both ideas could be true together

questions.text: Which belief do many Christians who oppose euthanasia use?

options: People should be free to choose when to die
Only God has the right to give and take life
Life began with the Big Bang
feedback: That is an argument used to support legalising assisted dying

questions.solution: Many Christians believe life is a gift from God, so only God should decide when it ends
questions.hint: Think about the sanctity of life

questions.text: Some people argue that legalising euthanasia could lead step by step to vulnerable people feeling pressured to die. What is this argument called? Give the term.
questions.solution: The slippery slope argument says one change could lead to more and more dangerous changes
questions.hint: It compares one step leading to worse steps down a hill

questions.text: Describe two ways religious believers might act as stewards of the environment.

rubric.model_answer: Many religious believers see themselves as stewards who must care for the Earth for God. They may cut their own pollution by recycling, saving energy and using public transport. They may also support or join environmental campaigns and charities; for example, many churches take part in the Eco Church scheme, and many Muslims see themselves as khalifah, trustees of the Earth for Allah.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one action (e.g. recycling, saving energy)
1 mark: links it to a religious belief
1 mark: identifies a second action (e.g. campaigns, Eco Church)
1 mark: links it to a religious belief

questions.solution: Believers can change their own lifestyle and support wider campaigns to protect creation
questions.hint: Think about everyday actions and group actions

questions.text: Which statement about religious views on the origins of the universe is accurate?

options: All religious people reject the Big Bang theory
The Big Bang theory was proposed by Charles Darwin
Science has proved God did not create the universe
Many Christians accept the Big Bang theory and believe God caused it

questions.solution: Many Christians, including the Catholic Church, accept the Big Bang as how God created the universe
questions.hint: Remember who first proposed the idea behind the Big Bang theory

questions.text: Which argument is used by people who SUPPORT legalising assisted dying?

options: People should have the right to choose to end unbearable suffering
Only God has the right to take life
It could put pressure on vulnerable people
feedback: That is an argument against
That is an argument against
That is an argument against

questions.solution: Supporters stress personal freedom (autonomy) and relieving suffering
questions.hint: Look for the argument about freedom of choice

questions.text: Why do many Hindus believe in treating animals with respect?

options: They believe animals rule over humans
They believe all living beings have an atman (soul)
They believe animals cannot feel pain
They believe animals exist only to be food

questions.solution: Many Hindus believe the atman is in every living being, so harming animals is wrong (ahimsa)
questions.hint: Think about what Hindus believe lives inside every creature

questions.text: Which statement about Christian beliefs about the afterlife is accurate?

options: Christians believe they will be reborn as animals
Christians believe the goal is moksha
Many Christians believe in resurrection, judgement, heaven and hell
Christians believe death is the end of all existence
feedback: Moksha is a Hindu belief about release from rebirth

questions.solution: Many Christians believe that after death God judges people, who are resurrected to heaven or hell
questions.hint: Think about what Christians believe happened to Jesus after his death

questions.text: A religious believer says: 'Testing medicines on animals can be justified, but testing cosmetics cannot.' Which idea is she using?

options: Animals must never be used by humans in any way
Humans may use animals for important needs but should avoid unnecessary suffering

questions.solution: She weighs the benefit to humans against the suffering caused, accepting it only for serious needs
questions.hint: Compare why medicines and cosmetics are tested

questions.text: Explain two religious beliefs about the sanctity of life.

rubric.model_answer: Many Christians believe life is sacred because humans are made in the image of God (Genesis 1:27), so every life has special value and must be protected. Many Christians and Muslims also believe God gives life and only God should decide when it ends; the Qur'an teaches that taking one innocent life is like taking the life of all humanity. This leads many believers to oppose euthanasia and abortion.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one belief (e.g. made in God's image)
1 mark: develops or applies it
1 mark: identifies a second belief (e.g. only God gives and takes life)
1 mark: develops or applies it

questions.solution: Believers see life as sacred because God creates it and humans are made in God's image
questions.hint: Think about where religious believers say life comes from

questions.text: What is the term for the belief that all war and violence is wrong? Give the term.
questions.solution: Pacifism is the belief that all violence and war is wrong
questions.hint: Quakers are well known for this belief

questions.text: Which Christian group is well known for its Peace Testimony and refusing to fight in wars?

feedback: The Crusaders fought religious wars in the Middle Ages

questions.solution: Quakers (the Religious Society of Friends) have a Peace Testimony and are known for pacifism
questions.hint: They are also called the Religious Society of Friends

questions.text: What does 'reconciliation' mean?

options: Starting a war for a religious cause
Restoring friendly relations after a conflict
feedback: That is a holy war
That is pacifism

questions.solution: Reconciliation means rebuilding a relationship after conflict or wrongdoing
questions.hint: Think of two sides making up after a quarrel

questions.text: What is the term for no longer feeling anger towards someone who has wronged you and not seeking revenge? Give the term.
questions.solution: Forgiveness means letting go of anger and the wish for revenge
questions.hint: Jesus taught that you should do this 'seventy times seven' times

questions.text: Which of these is an example of a weapon of mass destruction?
questions.solution: Weapons of mass destruction, such as nuclear, chemical and biological weapons, can destroy huge areas
questions.hint: Think about which weapon could destroy a whole city

questions.text: Which Indian leader used non-violent protest to campaign for independence from British rule? Give the surname.
questions.solution: Mohandas (Mahatma) Gandhi led non-violent campaigns, such as the Salt March of 1930
questions.hint: He led the Salt March in 1930

questions.text: Which statement describes a holy war?

options: A war that meets conditions such as last resort and proportionality
A refusal to fight in any war
A peace agreement after a conflict
A war fought for a religious cause, believed to be approved by God
feedback: That describes a just war
That is pacifism
That is a peace treaty or reconciliation

questions.solution: A holy war is fought for a religious reason, such as the Crusades in the Middle Ages
questions.hint: Think about the word holy

questions.text: Which Christian thinker first set out ideas about a just war, in the 4th and 5th centuries?

feedback: Martin Luther King lived in the 20th century and taught non-violence
John Wesley founded Methodism in the 18th century
St Francis lived in the 13th century and is linked with peace and care for creation

questions.solution: St Augustine of Hippo set out early just war ideas; Thomas Aquinas developed them later
questions.hint: He was a bishop in North Africa

questions.text: Which of these is a condition of just war theory?

options: War must be fought to gain land
War must be a last resort
War must make the attacking country rich
War can be declared by any group that wants to fight
feedback: Just war theory says war needs a proper (legitimate) authority

questions.solution: Just war theory says war must be a last resort, after peaceful ways have failed
questions.hint: Think about what should be tried before fighting

questions.text: What is the term for using violence, often against civilians, to create fear and achieve political or religious aims? Give the term.
questions.solution: Terrorism is the use of violence and fear to achieve aims; mainstream religious leaders condemn it
questions.hint: The word comes from the feeling of extreme fear

questions.text: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus says: 'Blessed are the ...' about people who work to bring peace. Give the missing word.
questions.solution: Jesus said 'Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God' (Matthew 5:9)
questions.hint: It is a compound word: the opposite of war plus people who make things

questions.text: The Arabic word 'salam' is part of many Muslim greetings. What does 'salam' mean?

feedback: Submission is the meaning of the word 'islam'
Prayer is salah
Pilgrimage is Hajj

questions.solution: Salam means peace; Muslims greet each other with 'As-salamu alaykum', peace be upon you
questions.hint: Muslims greet each other by wishing this upon one another

questions.text: A Christian refuses to join the army because Jesus taught 'love your enemies'. Which belief is he showing?
questions.solution: Refusing to fight because of Jesus' teaching on love is pacifism
questions.hint: He believes violence is always wrong

questions.text: A government declares war only after all peaceful talks have failed. Which just war condition does this meet?

feedback: Proportionality is about not using more force than needed

questions.solution: Going to war only after peaceful methods fail meets the condition of last resort
questions.hint: Think about the order things were tried in

questions.text: A country responds to a small border attack by destroying several enemy cities. Which just war condition does this break?
questions.solution: The response is far greater than the attack, so it breaks proportionality
questions.hint: Compare the size of the attack with the size of the response

questions.text: Which of these is an example of reconciliation?

options: Former enemies meeting to rebuild trust after a conflict

questions.solution: Reconciliation means rebuilding relationships, for example through meetings and peace projects
questions.hint: Look for the option where relationships are mended

questions.text: Which South African archbishop chaired the Truth and Reconciliation Commission after apartheid ended? Give the surname.
questions.solution: Archbishop Desmond Tutu chaired the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, set up in 1995
questions.hint: He won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1984

questions.text: Which American Baptist minister led non-violent protests for civil rights in the 1950s and 1960s? Give the full name.

feedback.Martin Luther: Martin Luther was a 16th-century German reformer; the civil rights leader's name is longer

questions.solution: Martin Luther King Jr used non-violent protest, inspired by Jesus and Gandhi
questions.hint: He gave the 'I have a dream' speech in 1963

questions.text: Jesus said: 'All they that take the sword shall perish with the sword' (Matthew 26:52). Which view does this verse support?
questions.solution: The verse warns that violence leads to more violence, so pacifists use it
questions.hint: Jesus said this when a follower used a sword to defend him

questions.text: Which argument is used by people who support nuclear deterrence?

options: Having nuclear weapons stops other countries from attacking
Nuclear weapons cannot tell soldiers and civilians apart
Nuclear weapons damage the environment for years
feedback: That is an argument against nuclear weapons
That is an argument against nuclear weapons
That is an argument against nuclear weapons

questions.solution: Deterrence means the threat of a nuclear response stops an enemy from attacking first
questions.hint: Deter means to put someone off doing something

questions.text: A rebel group starts a war without the approval of any government or ruler. Which just war condition is broken?
questions.solution: Just war theory says only a proper authority, such as a government, can declare war
questions.hint: Think about who has the right to declare war

questions.text: The Corrymeela Community in Northern Ireland brings Catholics and Protestants together. What does it work for?

options: Peace and reconciliation between divided communities

questions.solution: Corrymeela, founded in 1965, works for peace and reconciliation between communities in Northern Ireland
questions.hint: Think about the history of conflict in Northern Ireland

questions.text: Which phrase from the Sermon on the Mount tells Christians not to hit back if someone strikes them? Give the phrase.
questions.solution: Jesus taught that if someone strikes you on the right cheek, you should turn the other cheek too
questions.hint: It mentions a part of the face

questions.text: Describe two ways religious believers work for peace.

rubric.model_answer: Many believers pray for peace and take part in peace vigils or services, such as those on Remembrance Sunday. Some join organisations that work for reconciliation, for example the Corrymeela Community in Northern Ireland, which brings Catholics and Protestants together, or Pax Christi, a Catholic peace movement. Others give to charities that support victims of war, such as Christian Aid or Islamic Relief.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one way (e.g. prayer and vigils)
1 mark: supporting detail or example
1 mark: identifies a second way (e.g. peace organisations, charities)
1 mark: supporting detail or example

questions.solution: Believers pray, join peace organisations and support victims of war
questions.hint: Think about prayer, organisations and charities

questions.text: Which statement about Christian views on war is accurate?

options: All Christians believe every war is holy
No Christian has ever served in an army
Christians believe the Lord's Prayer commands war
Some Christians accept a just war, while others, such as Quakers, are pacifists

questions.solution: Christians disagree: many accept just war theory, while pacifist groups such as Quakers reject all war
questions.hint: Think about the difference between just war theory and pacifism

questions.text: Why do many religious believers oppose the use of nuclear weapons?

options: They cannot be used without harming huge numbers of innocent civilians
They are a form of pacifism
They were invented by religious leaders
They are banned by the Five Pillars

questions.solution: Nuclear weapons cannot tell soldiers and civilians apart, and their effects are out of proportion
questions.hint: Think about the just war conditions on protecting civilians and proportionality

questions.text: Which statement about forgiveness in Christianity and Islam is accurate?

options: Both teach that forgiveness is never possible
Both teach that God is forgiving and that believers should forgive others
Both teach that forgiveness means there should be no justice
feedback: Both religions teach that forgiveness and justice can go together

questions.solution: Christians follow Jesus' teaching to forgive, and Muslims believe Allah is merciful and forgiving
questions.hint: Think about what both religions teach about God's mercy

questions.text: Which statement about religious views on protest is accurate?

options: Many religious believers support peaceful protest but oppose violence
Christianity teaches that violent protest is a sacrament

questions.solution: Many believers, like Martin Luther King, support peaceful protest against injustice but reject violence
questions.hint: Think about how Gandhi and Martin Luther King protested

questions.text: Which statement about terrorism is accurate according to mainstream religious teaching?

options: Terrorism counts as a just war
Terrorism is a type of pacifism
Mainstream Christian and Muslim leaders condemn attacks on innocent people

questions.solution: Mainstream religious leaders condemn terrorism because it targets innocent people
questions.hint: Think about the just war rule on protecting civilians

questions.text: Explain two religious teachings about forgiveness.

rubric.model_answer: Christians follow Jesus' teaching that they should forgive 'seventy times seven' times, meaning without limit, and in the Lord's Prayer they ask God to 'forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive them that trespass against us'. Muslims believe Allah is merciful and forgiving, and the Qur'an encourages believers to pardon others and make peace. Both teach that forgiveness does not mean ignoring justice.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one teaching (e.g. seventy times seven)
1 mark: explains what it means for believers
1 mark: identifies a second teaching (e.g. Lord's Prayer, Allah is merciful)
1 mark: explains what it means for believers

questions.solution: Christianity and Islam both teach that God forgives and that believers should forgive others
questions.hint: Think about what Jesus said about how often to forgive
